problems.title: Real-mode throws claim the ground gives way, using the nominal isometric force: up to '140 septillion× its limit' for a baseball. Regression from the sink-check change.
problems.evidence: M3's own repro: Real muscle, granite, Claws dug in, 10³⁴ kg, Throw baseball 45°. The chips read 'Footing holds | Ground gives way under his feet'. The bullet reads 'the ground under him is carrying 140 septillion× its limit, so he sinks while he throws.' The push lasts 26 ms, and the average force on the ball is pB/t ≈ 2.2 kN against the 153 MN granite limit. Common case: Real muscle, Hulk (default), concrete, Throw shot 45°. That shows 'Ground gives way… carrying 1.5× its limit', while the average push is 8.1 kN against a 225 kN limit. Real Hulk baseball on sand shows '2× its limit' for a 0.2 kg ball. Cause: throwOnce computes sinkRatio = anc.N(Fused)/Nmax with Fused = F, the full Hill F0, whenever he doesn't hold back. Real muscle only exerts F0 at zero speed, for well under a millisecond. The jump on the same page uses the dynamic sink (push.xB > 1 mm) and says granite holds. The previous code used min(F, R), which never produced this.
problems.fix: In real mode, base the sink check on the force actually applied: use the work-averaged force push.work/(push.xA+push.xB), or the integrator's force after its first step, in place of the nominal F. Better, apply the jump's dynamic criterion (bearing plus ρv² inertia, sink > 1 mm). Keep the nominal force for comic mode, where the force is constant over the stroke.

- **Hulk, sand, baseball.** It shows "2× its limit" (1.95).

The integrator's own implicit steps never apply anything close to it at high strength. In the 10^34 granite case the largest force any step applies is 3.3 MN, while F0 is 2.9e34 N.

- **Granite 10^34 baseball:** the push lasts 26 ms. The mean force is pB/t ≈ 2.2 kN (work-averaged 1.1 kN), against Nmax = 153 MN. The real foot-load ratio is about 2e-5.
- **Hulk concrete shot:** the push lasts 48 ms with pB/t ≈ 8.1 kN, against Nmax = 225 kN. The ratio is 0.034.

Concrete shot with claws dug in reads 161× at 10^7 kg and 1.6e29× at 10^34 kg; time-averaged, both are about 0.035. When he holds back, the cap multiples make the value jump around too (concrete baseball, claws dug in, 10^12 kg reads 5.81).

Comic mode is not affected: there the force is constant, and pB/t + RB equals F exactly. I checked this numerically for the shot and the car.

I could not check the claim that this is a regression, because there is no history in the folder. It does not affect whether the problem is real.

It does this for everyday Real-mode setups, such as Hulk throwing a shot on concrete, and it contradicts the jump and the Footing chip. The owner ranks accuracy and honest labelling first.

Base the foot load on the mean push over the stroke, impulse divided by time, rather than nominal F0. This number equals F exactly in comic mode, so one line covers both modes.

In throwOnce (src/engine.js, just before line 699):

    // Load on his feet: mean push over the stroke (impulse/time). In comic mode this equals F; real muscle hits F0 only for an instant at zero speed.
    const Fload = isFinite(Fused) && !push.stalled && push.t > 0 && isFinite(push.pB) ? Math.min(Fused, push.pB / push.t + RB) : Fused;
    const Nfeet = isFinite(Fload) ? anc.N(Fload) : (Math.sin(th) > 1e-12 ? Infinity : anc.N(0));

I applied this to a scratch copy of the engine:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Real, granite, claws dug in, 10^34 kg, baseball | 1.4e26 | 2.2e-5 (ground holds) |
| Real, Hulk, concrete, shot | 1.47 | 0.034 (ground holds) |
| Real, Hulk, sand, baseball | 1.95 | 1.33 |

The sand case still shows "gives way". That is reasonable: standing alone already loads sand to 0.77 of its limit, so the throw really does overload it for the whole stroke.

Sustained heavy pushes are almost unchanged, for example the concrete tank at 3.52 before and after. Comic-mode values are identical: concrete shot 0.478, concrete car 0.977, sand car 98.3.

  const Fpalm = Math.hypot(Fused, perp);   // equals Fdrive when he doesn't hold back; Infinity stays Infinity
  ...
  gripRatio: obj.crush ? Fpalm / contact / obj.crush : 0,

In the `show` function of renderLadder (src/app.html:1246-1248), replace the two top-calculation lines so the tip is placed against the focused g's measured box, using the tip's real height:

```js
const gr = g2.getBoundingClientRect(), th = tip.offsetHeight;
let top = gr.bottom - rect.top + 6;                                          // below the whole marker
if (top + th > rect.height) top = Math.max(0, gr.top - rect.top - 6 - th);   // else fully above it
```
